newsitem.title: INDIA: India court keeps Gandhi wedding plans in suspense.
newsitem.headline: India court keeps Gandhi wedding plans in suspense.

text.p: An Indian court said it would decide on Wednesday if the daughter of former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi can go ahead with her planned wedding next month after a man claimed she was already his wife.

The Press Trust of India (PTI) said Civil Judge Vipin Gupta delayed the decision he was due to give on Tuesday after V. Ramakrishna Goud made "some additional submissions" to the court to support his claim of marriage to Priyanka Gandhi, 25.
Gandhi, often regarded as her father's political heir, has denied Goud's claim "maliciously false, concocted and outrageous," PTI said.
Gandhi made the plea through her lawyers and was not present in the court.

She told Gupta that she planned to marry Delhi businessman Robert Wadhera on February 5. Goud asked the court to stop the wedding pending a decision on his plea that because he married her in Delhi in November 1991 she could not wed again.
Gupta recorded Goud's statement and said he would have them verified by "appropiate authorities", PTI said.
Gupta on Monday threw out a plea in which Goud sought a medical examination of Gandhi which he said would prove they had married in 1991.
Goud himself was brought to Gupta's court under judicial custody in a separate case. He is accused of using offensive language against low-caste Hindus in his southern state of Andhra Pradesh.

After Rajiv Gandhi was killed by a woman suicide bomber in May 1991, senior leaders of his Congress party turned to his Italian-born widow Sonia Gandhi to become the party's president. But the media-shy and self-effacing Sonia Gandhi has kept largely aloof from public life.

Some newspapers have said that Priyanka Gandhi, whom they liken to her grandmother and former prime minister Indira Gandhi, was the next choice for the Congress to keep the Nehru-Gandhi dynasty in the country's political limelight.
Priyanka Gandhi has a 27-year old brother. But Congress sources say he is not interested in politics.
